definitions.explanation: The very beginning or opening part of a speech, text, story, or event. Emphasizes the first portion rather than a point in time.

examples.japanese: {冒頭|ぼうとう}で{述|の}べたように。
{小説|しょうせつ}の{冒頭|ぼうとう}が{印象的|いんしょうてき}だった。
examples.english: The opening of the novel was impressive.

examples.japanese: {映画|えいが}の{冒頭|ぼうとう}シーンで{観客|かんきゃく}の{心|こころ}をつかんだ。
examples.english: The opening scene of the film captured the audience's hearts.

notes:
Compound of {冒|ぼう} (to risk, to brave) + {頭|とう} (head, beginning). Refers specifically to the opening portion of something structured like a text, speech, or performance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {冒頭|ぼうとう}で (at the beginning)
- {冒頭|ぼうとう}に (at the start)
- {冒頭|ぼうとう}シーン (opening scene)
- {冒頭|ぼうとう}{部分|ぶぶん} (opening section)
- {冒頭|ぼうとう}{陳述|ちんじゅつ} (opening statement)

USAGE:
{冒頭|ぼうとう} refers to the opening portion of something, not merely the start time. It is often used with texts ({小説|しょうせつ}, {論文|ろんぶん}), speeches ({演説|えんぜつ}, {挨拶|あいさつ}), and performances ({映画|えいが}, {番組|ばんぐみ}). It has a somewhat formal tone and is common in written Japanese and news broadcasts.

cross_references.notes: 暴騰 means a sharp rise (in prices) — same reading, different meaning
